summary: Announces that the Stanford Electronics Research Lab host SU-DSL, a Very Distant Host, changes from IMP 2 Host 2 to IMP 2 Host 3, moving its address from 130 to 194.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 637 announces that SU-DSL moved from Host 2 to Host 3 on IMP 2. Its network address changed from 130 to 194, effective immediately.

questions: what was the new network address for su dsl
subtitle: A notice that the SU-DSL host's network address changed immediately.

tldr.problem: The Stanford Electronics Research Lab's SU-DSL host was reassigned from Host 2 to Host 3 on IMP 2.
tldr.mechanism: The notice changes its network address from 130 to 194, effective immediately.
tldr.outcome: The old IMP 2 Host 2 position would eventually be used by a PDP-11 operated by the SRI Artificial Intelligence Center.

today: RFC 637 is an operational notice of a 1974 SU-DSL network-address change.

sections.title: SU-DSL's New Address
sections.content: The SU-DSL host at Stanford Electronics Research Lab, a Very Distant Host connected to the SRI IMP, changed from IMP 2, Host 2 to IMP 2, Host 3. The RFC says the corresponding network address changed from 130 to 194, effective immediately.
sections.plainLanguage: SU-DSL stayed on IMP 2 but moved from Host 2 to Host 3. The new network address is 194 instead of 130.

sections.title: Use of the Previous Host Position
sections.content: The notice says Host 2 on IMP 2 would eventually be a PDP-11 operated by the SRI Artificial Intelligence Center. It provides no further details about the reassignment or its timing.
sections.plainLanguage: The previous position was expected to be used by an SRI Artificial Intelligence Center PDP-11.

sections.title: Effective Immediately
sections.content: The address change took effect immediately according to the RFC. The notice identifies the former and new host positions and network addresses.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC announces an immediate address change and gives both the old and new values.
